findings.title: Overlapping refresh could restore an obsolete local quota cache
findings.description: Adding a background caller exposes refresh-versus-pairing/demo and compare-versus-write races. The shared revision coordinator now rejects obsolete responses and serializes monotonic cache commits; local tests passed, not yet merged.

steps.detail: Authenticate/decode the snapshot, then compare with the current channel/sequence cache under a guarded revision commit.

sink.impact: An obsolete local quota projection could otherwise be restored after disconnect, re-pair or demo mode.

mitigations: Shared revision invalidation for pairing, disconnect and local demo changes
Atomic compare/write under the same lock; network I/O remains outside it
Unit tests for stale-response rejection and concurrent monotonic commits
findings.attacker_story: A delayed relay reply overlaps a local pairing/mode change. Without a revision guard it could restore the previous projection, but cannot expose vendor credentials or bypass AES-GCM.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep all pairing/cache mutations and response commits on SnapshotRefreshCoordinator; verify physical lifecycle behavior before distribution.
findings.resolved_by: Working changes and local unit tests
